events.text: You have lain under this ford for two hundred years, and the snake says two hundred and six. Things go over. Things fall in. The old turtles still tell it: a prince on a riverbank, with the horsemen behind him, and every back in the water coming up at once. "It was a great mistake," the snake says. "We were sat on by a horse." You have thought it over since then. You find that you remember the weight.

choices.text: The next one the river takes, rise

effects.log: The snake sighs, and it starts a new count. You shift your feet in the silt, a little nearer to the deep part of the ford. It takes you the whole of a winter. There is no hurry. Somebody always falls in.

choices.text: No. What is carried is yours, and you have no use for it

effects.log: "Thank you," says the snake. You go on lying there. The silt comes up over your plates, and nobody is sat on, and it is a very peaceful century. The snake is bored by the end of the first week.

events.text: An ox driver goes off the stones in the spring melt, drunk, singing, with his hat on. You are almost under him. You come up, and his boots find something, and he stands there in the fast water, a little surprised, up to his belt. On the bank he wrings out his hat. "Still got it," he tells the ox. He has always been a strong swimmer. "He has never swum in his life," says the snake, delighted.

choices.text: Sink back, content. So that is what it is like

effects.log: It weighs next to nothing. You think about it for a long time. By the time you are done thinking, the snake says, he has had grandchildren, and they have all been told about the time that he swam the ford.

choices.text: Let the snake put its head up, and tell him the truth

effects.log: "You owe me," the snake says, from the water, in a voice like a wet rope. He falls down on the bank. He does not come that way again, and nor does the ox. The snake considers that this was money well spent.

events.text: There is a woman on the far side of the river, calling. It may be a child that she is calling. You turn your head and you begin. It is a long way across for you, with the current, and you do not hurry, you have never been able to find out how, and the snake is saying things that you have not heard it say before. You get there. It is a fine clear morning. There is a straw sandal going round in the eddy.

choices.text: Stay where you are. Lie in that eddy, from now on

effects.log: You do not know how long you lie there. "Eleven years," says the snake, quietly. Nobody else is lost from that bend in those eleven years, and you have never asked the snake what it would have done.

choices.text: Tell the snake that it could not have been helped

effects.log: It does not say anything. It does not say anything at all until the thaw. You turn it over a good deal, in the dark, and you find that the two of you are not going to agree about it.

events.text: A thief comes into the water at a run, at dusk, with a very good silver bowl and men with torches behind him. He cannot swim either. He goes under right above you. "We do not have to," says the snake. "What it carries is its own. Think about what you would be getting." Your back has started to come up. It seems to have made up its mind.

choices.text: Carry him. To the far side, slowly, with the torches watching

effects.log: They stand on the bank, quite still, and they do not throw anything. On the far side he kisses the ground, and he never steals again, for a whole month. He is yours now. You will hear about him. "I told you," says the snake.

choices.text: Let the snake have its way, this once. Lie still

effects.log: They find him downstream, with the bowl. You did nothing whatever. It is exactly what you have done every day for two hundred years. So you cannot think why it should taste of anything.

events.text: You took {npc} off the ford in the bad water, and put {him} on the landing stone, and thought no more of it. {He} has come down to the stone every tenth day since, and sits on it with {his} feet in the river, and eats. "I know that you are down there," {he} says to the water. "I would like to know what I owe. I do not like to owe." The snake has started to look forward to it.

choices.text: Come up a little, by the stone. Let {him} see the back

effects.log: You rise as far as the third plate. {He} stops chewing, and {he} looks at you for a long time. "Well," {he} says. {He} breaks off a bit of rice cake, and {he} holds it out. The snake takes it. It has never been so happy.

choices.text: Lie still. It will stop. They all stop

effects.log: You lie still. {He} comes on the tenth day and on the twentieth. Then {he} does not. "There," says the snake. It sounds out of temper. "Thirty-one years, and that is the last you will hear of that." You had not known it was thirty-one.

events.text: {npc} has asked you a question. Are you cold in the winter? You think about it. You turn it over on the river bed, and you consider what cold has been, and the ways it has changed. You have got your answer nearly ready, and you rise by the stone to give it. {He} is sitting there. {His} hair is a different length, and {he} has a new coat. "Three years," the snake says. "I did tell you."

choices.text: Nod. Yes, you are cold in the winter

effects.log: {He} looks at you in some puzzlement, and then {he} remembers, and {he} starts to laugh, and has to hold on to the stone. "Oh," {he} says. "Oh, you are a slow one. Ask me something, then." So now you have to think of a question.

choices.text: Have the snake answer in future. It is quicker

effects.log: So the snake does the talking. It tells {him} about cold, and about the price of carp, and it has a number of opinions. {He} is very well entertained, and you lie there underneath the two of them. You are not at all sure that this is what you meant.

events.text: The snake has been looking at {npc} sidelong, as it looks at the sky before ice. The snake reads ends. It has seen it on {him}, plain as a mark on a post, and it has stopped its chatter. "I can tell you the year," it says, under the water, where {he} will not hear. "It would be a help to you. You have never seen anything coming. It is not so far off as you would think."

choices.text: Tell it no. Press your head down until it is quiet

effects.log: It is the first time that you have ever pulled against it. It takes a season, and it hurts all along the shell. "As you like," says the snake. "But I will know. I will sit here and know it, every day, next to you." You had not thought about that.

choices.text: Let it tell you

effects.log: It tells you. It is only a number. You lie on the bed of the river, and you hold it, and you find you have no idea how long that is. You ask the snake. It explains. You go on not knowing how long that is, and now you are afraid.

events.text: {npc} has climbed down onto the landing stone with a jar and two cups. {He} is sitting with one hand on your second plate, which nobody has done. "I have no idea what this is," {he} says. "But I have got nobody else that I tell things. So here is what I will do. I will come to this stone for as long as I have legs, and tell you the news. And you will be here. Is that all right?" The snake has opened its mouth.

choices.text: Hold the snake's head down, and bring yours up. Lay your chin on the stone

effects.log: Your chin comes down on the stone, by {his} foot, with a small wet sound. {He} drinks {his} cup, and pours the other over your head. It is the strongest thing to have happened to you in a thousand years. "Well, that is done," {he} says. "Now, about the miller."

choices.text: Let the snake say it: {he} will be dead by the time that you have finished nodding

effects.log: It says so, quite gently, for the snake. {npc} sits there with the two cups. Then {he} drinks them both, one after the other, and goes up the bank. {He} does not look back. You are still thinking about it some time after the bank has gone.

events.text: It is a good system. Every tenth day, {npc} comes down to the stone and tells you who has died and who owes what. "You have no idea who that is," says the snake. "That is the grandson." You are sure that you heard about a boy called Chil-bok, with big ears, who fell out of a tree. Chil-bok came to the stone last month, with a stick. You have blinked, it seems.

choices.text: Ask how that boy is doing, with the tree

effects.log: You nod at the tree. It takes a while. {He} works it out in the end. "Chil-bok is fine," says {npc}, and pats your nose. "It has healed nicely." {He} does not tell you anything more about Chil-bok. It is not for a long time that you notice.

choices.text: Get the snake to keep it all straight for you, year by year

effects.log: It does. It has it all by name and date. You have it read to you under the ice, all of the village, like a very long sum. You find that it is much worse, and you ask it to go on.

events.text: Somebody from the magistrate's office is standing on the stone. A person of this village, it seems, has been crossing the river for years without paying the toll. {npc} is looking at the sky. "On what?" says the clerk. You come up a little. The clerk looks down between the clerk's feet, takes out a brush, considers the regulations, and looks up. "Is that a vessel?"

choices.text: Let the snake take the clerk through the regulations

effects.log: It lasts for nine days. The snake knows every toll on that river since the old kingdom, and who waived them. The clerk has the time of a lifetime. The office enters you as a fixed bridge, under repair. You have been under repair, officially, for two hundred years.

choices.text: Lift one foot out of the water, slowly, and put it down on the stone

effects.log: It is a large foot. There is a long silence. The clerk writes something down, and thanks {npc} for {his} time. {He} tells you it is the first thing that {he} has ever seen you do in less than a year, and that {he} is very proud.

events.text: It is a warm evening, and for no reason {npc} wants to go across. {He} has done this a thousand times. "Nine thousand and four," says the snake. {He} takes {his} sandals off, and sits on the fifth plate with {his} feet hanging. You set off. You like this best of all. The river goes by on both sides. You are about the speed of the shadow of a hill.

choices.text: Go slower. Stretch it out until the stars are up

effects.log: {He} goes to sleep halfway over, with {his} mouth open. You stop altogether, in the middle of the river, and hold quite still. There are carp going by. You could not say how long that lasts, and for once the snake does not tell you.

choices.text: Take {him} over, and turn back. {He} has things to do

effects.log: You get {him} home by dark. {He} has things to do. {He} has hens, and a roof. "Three hours you have saved {him}," says the snake, "out of what is left." You had asked it never to tell you that, and it has not told you. It has only said three hours.

events.text: You were two bends down for the eel run. {npc} is standing on the stone. {He} has a ferry pole in both hands. There was a flood on the upper ford, with children on the rope, and {he} stood on this stone for nine days calling, and you were two bends down. "Where were you?" {he} says. You begin to think about it. {He} lifts the pole. You have told {him} one thing, and it was never to do this.

choices.text: Take it. Then have the snake tell {him} what {he} has done

effects.log: It rings. Every fish in the river turns. It goes on ringing for a day, and diviners will have heard it as far off as the capital. "That was the shell," says the snake, for once very quiet. "They will come now." {He} drops the pole. {He} sits down in the water with you, and {he} stays.

choices.text: Sink before it lands. Go down, and do not come back to this stone

effects.log: It hits the water, and the water closes. You go down into the deep with your head in. {He} is calling you things from up there, very faint, for most of a season. There is not a thing in the world that is slower than you, and you go.

choices.text: Turn the snake on {him}. A strike at the pole, not at {him}. It is all the warning you have

effects.log: The pole goes spinning off. There is a long red mark across {his} knuckles. {He} looks at it, and at the snake, whose eyes are quite flat. {He} comes back on the tenth day, and {he} tells you the news, in a very small voice. It is never the same.

events.text: {npc} is lying on {his} back on the stone. {He} has been trading insults with the snake for most of {his} life. "You know," {he} says. "All these years. I call the big one Slow. What do I call you? You must have a name." The river goes quiet. It has never, in nine hundred years, been anyone but the other half of you. The snake turns to look at {him}.

choices.text: Let it answer. It has waited long enough for someone to ask

effects.log: It says a word. It is very short, and you have never heard it. It goes through you from the tail to the head, like a cold wire. You cannot feel it, for a moment, where it wraps you. "That is nice," says {npc}, who knows nothing. The snake is shaking.

choices.text: Take {him} up in your slowest voice, and say the only thing you ever have: no

effects.log: It takes you until the moon is down to say it. It may be the first word that you have ever spoken to {him} yourself. {He} sits up. {He} has gone quite pale, and it is a good while before {he} laughs. {He} does not ask that again. The snake does not thank you.

choices.text: Go. Sink, with {him} on the stone and the question in the air, and do not come up

effects.log: You take the snake down with you. It looks back the whole way. {He} calls for a while, not understanding, then {he} calls the snake by nothing at all. You have kept your whole self, and it has not spoken to you since.

events.text: The river in flood brings all sorts of things. A wash-tub, going round in the brown water, very low, with something wrapped up in the bottom of it and yelling. It is the first thing that you have ever not thought about. You are under it before the snake has finished speaking. You lay it against the stone, and {npc} looks in. "That is {bk_child}," {he} says. {He} has just decided.

choices.text: Stay by the stone, all that night, with your back against the tub

effects.log: {He} has got it inside {his} coat, and {he} sits down on your plates. It screams for hours. "Nobody will come for that," says the snake. "I have looked." What it carries is its own. Well, you carried it. You can feel that going in, slowly, for the next few years.

choices.text: Have the snake ask along the river whose it is

effects.log: It asks. It asks for a whole spring, of everything that has a mouth. It comes back with a burned village and no name. {npc} has already got a cradle made. "You knew that," {he} says, to the snake, and it does not deny it.

events.text: {npc} has found a black stone in the shallows, the shape of an egg, and set it on the landing with a bowl of rice. {He} is singing at it, the song the children know: "Turtle, turtle, put forth your head. If you will not, we will roast you and eat you." "That is a rock," says the snake. In the morning there is a bundle by that stone, left by someone who could not feed it. It is {bk_child}. {He} looks very smug.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let {him} think so

effects.log: {He} tells everyone. You lie there, and hear how you laid an egg. The snake is not speaking to either of you. Whoever left it never does come back. {He} has put the rock on the shelf, and every year on that day {he} sings at it.

choices.text: Have the snake point out how eggs work, at length

effects.log: {He} listens to all of it, joggling the bundle. "You have never had any faith," {he} says. It goes on for most of a year. The child takes its first steps during the second part of the argument, on your back, and it is holding on to the snake.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven now, and hates the river. {bk_child} has been building a boat from three boards and a door, and it has sunk twice. Being carried is for babies. {bk_child} sits on the stone with skinned knees, swearing at some carp. {bk_love} says it is a very good sign. The snake has looked at that child from all sides. "A cold in the head," it says. "Nothing more. Eighty years at the outside."

choices.text: Tell the snake that eighty years will do

effects.log: You get it done by spring. It is a fine thing to be able to say. {bk_child} has made the crossing on the door by then, most of the way, and walks home from the far bank soaked and very pleased, not looking at you.

choices.text: Rise a little under the door, on the next try, where nobody can tell

effects.log: It goes across very nicely. {bk_child} stands on the far bank with both fists in the air. You sink back. You are going to do that for as long as it lasts. You do not need the snake to tell you what that will be called.

events.text: {bk_love} goes down at the ford in the spring melt, and you are a long bend away. The snake screams at you. You go as you go, and when you get there you are too late. {bk_child}, who is seven, is in the river to the chin, with {bk_love} across that small back, walking. Not fast. The water goes round. For the first time in your life the snake has nothing to say.

choices.text: Come up under them both, and take the weight. Let {bk_child} keep walking

effects.log: You come up very slowly, an inch under those small feet. {bk_child} looks down and nods, as one does to a fellow ferryman, and goes on. On the stone {bk_love} coughs and weeps and holds on. {bk_child} would like some food now. That one is not going to hurry for anyone, ever.

choices.text: Stay down. Let it finish what it began

effects.log: It takes the rest of the afternoon. You follow along below, where nobody can see, with your nose a hand from those heels, and you are not needed. It is the worst thing and the finest that you have ever watched. "How long?" you ask the snake. "A very long time," it says, and it sounds afraid.

events.text: You have turned over in your sleep, and you come up by the stone. There is an old person on it. {He} has very little hair, and no teeth to speak of, and {he} has been carried down here by a grandchild, who is sitting up on the bank and looking bored. "You took your time," says {npc}. It is the voice. You look to the snake. "I told you," it says. It is not gloating. "I told you every year. You kept saying yes."

choices.text: Take {him} across. As slowly as you know how

effects.log: {He} is hardly any weight at all. It takes a day and a night, and you stop for the stars. {He} tells you about the miller, who has been dead for forty years, and you know the miller. It is the first time that you have been up to date.

choices.text: Lay your chin on the stone, and ask the snake what year it is

effects.log: "Do not," it says. You ask. So it tells you, and you put that beside the other number, the one that it told you, or the one that you would not hear. {He} has got {his} hand on your nose, and {he} does not seem to know what the two of you are talking about, and that is a mercy.

events.text: You have come up by the stone with something to tell {bk_love}. You have been working on it. There is moss on the stone. There is no one there, and there is a young willow, which is new. You lie there for a time. You ask the snake when the tenth day is. "{bk_love} died," it says. "Nine years ago, in the autumn, at the house. I told you. You said, yes, in a moment."

choices.text: Lay your chin on the stone, and tell it anyway

effects.log: It takes you until the ice. It is not very long, when it is said. The snake does not interrupt. It tells you afterward that you got one of the names wrong, and then it stops, and it is quiet for some years.

choices.text: Have it read the count. Every crossing, by number, from the first

effects.log: It goes through all of them under the ice, for four winters, in a low voice. It has the weather for each one. It has what was said about the miller. You had no idea that it had been keeping that. You had thought it was keeping score.

events.text: There is a ferry at this crossing now, and it is very slow. The family has had it since anyone can remember, and they do not charge you the first time, and they will wait for anyone at all. They have a black rock on a shelf in the ferry house. On the first day of spring they sing at it, and then, looking a little foolish, they sing it at the water.

choices.text: Put forth your head. It is only polite

effects.log: You rise by the stone, a long way off, with the mist on you. A small one sees it, and pulls at a sleeve, and is told not to point. They all go on singing. It is much too flat. "Roast you and eat you," they sing, happily, and you are so proud.

choices.text: Stay under their keel, on the bad days. They need not know

effects.log: They have never lost anyone. It is the finest record on the river, and they put it down to going slowly. "Which it is," says the snake. You lie under them as the boat goes across, about the speed of a hill.

events.text: A small war has come up the river. One of {bk_child}'s people is on the bank, an aged clerk of some sort, sitting on a box of records and eating lunch. There is a burned town behind them. Soldiers have told them to run. They finish their rice. They look up at the man with the spear, who has been shouting for a while, as if he had just arrived.

choices.text: Rise behind them. Put your head up out of the river, and let him look

effects.log: He stops shouting. He stares over that small grey head, and his mouth is open, and he goes away. The clerk has not turned round. They close the lunch box. "Yes, thank you," they say, in a mild voice, to nobody.

choices.text: Stay down. You have an idea how this one comes out

effects.log: They talk to him. It lasts for hours. He ends up carrying the box. "That," says the snake, with great satisfaction, "is the first thing that family has ever got from me."

events.text: Someone has sat on you. You had come up for the sun, by the old stone, and {npc} has climbed on with a groan, under the impression that you are a rock. {He} is a very old salt peddler. {He} eats, complains about the road, goes on, and comes back the same time next spring and the next. "Do not," says the snake. "You have not even been properly introduced." You stay out in the sun.

choices.text: Say something. It has only taken you three springs

effects.log: You move your head and you look round at {him}. {He} looks at you, and goes on chewing. "I wondered when you would get to that," {he} says. "It is a nice warm rock, and I have only got a few years. Are you going to make a fuss?" The snake gives up.

choices.text: Go. Move twenty li downstream, before the next spring

effects.log: It takes six years, in the end. You do not hurry. You come to a good deep bend. On the bank, a long time later, you hear that a peddler has stopped coming along that road. "I could have told you the year," says the snake. You do not ask.

events.text: Someone is on the bank, and you only notice because they have been there for some time. They have sat down with their hands on their knees and are looking at the water, as if it had just arrived. "That has been forty days," the snake says, disturbed. "They have not moved. Nobody does that. Nobody has ever done that but you." It has started looking up, every so often, as you do.

choices.text: Come up. In your own good time. Let them have the first word

effects.log: It takes you till the leaves are off. They look you over, and they nod. Neither of you has anything to say. They have been told that it was you who started this, and they thought they would come and see how it is done properly.

choices.text: Let the snake lose. See how long it holds out

effects.log: It holds out for fifty-two days, and then it goes up and it starts to talk. It tells them everything. They listen, with great politeness, to all of it, and then they go home. It is much the best laugh that you have ever had, and it takes you nine years to have it.

events.text: The house is shouting. The roof of the shed has caught, and everyone is running with buckets. You are six, and you are finishing your rice, because you have not finished it yet. {npc}, an old friend of the house, comes in for the bigger pot, and looks at you in the middle of it all, chewing. You look up at {him}, and you wonder what the hurry is.

choices.text: Ask {him}. What is the hurry?

effects.log: {npc} starts to laugh, with the pot in {his} hands, and the house on fire behind {him}. "Nothing, I suppose," {he} says, and {he} goes back out. It is a very small fire, in the end. You have got to the bottom of your bowl by then.

choices.text: Put down the spoon, and run, and shout, like the others

effects.log: You run, and you shout. You have seen how it is done. You get to the well some time after the fire is out, and everybody is very pleased with you for trying. It was a lot of trouble, and you do not see that it changed anything.

events.text: At ten you fall out of the Chos' pear tree, from the very top, on to the road, in front of a loaded cart. {npc} sees all of it. There is a noise, and the axle has gone. You are lying on your back, and you have been looking at some clouds. Your shirt is torn. You sit up after a time. {npc} has very slowly lifted your shirt to have a look at your back, and {he} has let it down again.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} saw there

effects.log: "You will want to keep your shirt on," says {npc}, "at the river." Then {he} goes to help with the axle. You try to see it in the water at home. It is only your back. It may be that the bones are a little wide, and that they have a pattern to them.

choices.text: Groan, and be carried home, and stay in bed a week

effects.log: You have to be reminded to groan. {npc} sits by you, feeding you soup, and looking at the wall. The carter comes to ask how you are, with a hat in both hands. You pay for the axle, out of your savings, for the rest of that year.

events.text: You have started to lose arguments with yourself. You are fourteen, and you should go down to the market. "Yes," says something, slowly. "In a while." Something else, quick and cold, just behind your ear, says that the salt man is cheating you by a fifth, and that the old pear tree comes down in the third storm from now. It is right about the salt man. You say so, aloud, and {npc} looks up from {his} sandals.

choices.text: Ask {him} if everyone has two

effects.log: "No," says {npc}. {He} waxes {his} thread. "Which of them told you to ask?" You have to think about that. You have to think about it for rather a long time. By the time you have got an answer, {he} has gone in.

choices.text: Tell them both to be quiet, and go to the market

effects.log: You go. You pay the salt man. The Bak girl laughs. On the way home you take a long way round, away from the pear tree, for no reason at all. It is a very quiet walk, and you do not believe it for a moment.

events.text: You are sixteen, and you went in the north river on a hot day to get cool. It is colder than it should be. You stand in it up to your neck. Your breath slows down. A leaf goes by you, and then it is a different leaf, and the bank has gone a different colour. {npc} is shaking you by the ear, in a straw coat. "It is the ninth month," {he} says. "We held the funeral. Come out, and I will tell you who carried whom."

choices.text: Come out, and sit by the fire, and hear it

effects.log: A river in flood, and a child called {bk_line}, and a back that came up under them. {bk_anc}, whatever that is, and {he} says it is a good many things. What it carries is its own. You sit by the fire and you cannot get warm. You have never felt so much at home.

choices.text: Say that you only came for a swim

effects.log: "You did," says {npc}, and {he} hits you, and hands you a dry coat. It is the first time that you have seen {him} cry. There is a mound with your name on it, up on the hill, and you help them dig it out. You are very sorry about it, as soon as you can get to that.

events.text: There has been a matchmaker. The matchmaker sat in the good room, with a list, and asked you what you thought of the Oh family's second child, and you said that you would think about it. That was the spring before last. The Oh family's second child has since married, and had twins. {npc} tells you this, over the fence. The matchmaker has been heard to use language.

choices.text: Go round and apologise. Learn to answer within the week

effects.log: You make a practice of it. You stand in the yard with a stick, and you say yes or no to things. It is very hard. People start to find you almost normal, and you are always a little out of breath.

choices.text: Send word that you have finished thinking, and that it was a good idea

effects.log: They laugh about that for a generation, in three villages. They tell it in the wine-house. You do not see what is so funny. The matchmaker has you on a list of the matchmaker's own. You are not at all sorry, and you are in no hurry.

events.text: The ice is going out, and the ferry has gone with it. There are eleven people on a shoal, in the middle of the river, and the shoal is getting smaller. Everyone on the bank is shouting about ropes. You have noticed that you are taking your shoes off. {npc} has hold of your sleeve. "Not in front of people," {he} says. "They will not forget it."

choices.text: Walk in, on the bottom if you have to. Bring them back, one at a time

effects.log: It takes all that day. They hold on to your shoulders and they do not look at you. The water goes round. You come out at the end of it with your lips blue, and you are not even breathing hard, and there is a good deal of talk.

choices.text: Help with the rope, like anyone. Be a good strong pair of hands

effects.log: You haul with the others. They get seven off, and it is a great victory, and they buy you a bowl of hot tea. You sit with your hands around it. You do not need anyone to tell you the number, for you can hear it being said behind your ear.

events.text: It is the Cho boy's funeral. The boy was seventy-one. You went to school together. You stand at the side, with your good black hair and your smooth face, and the grandchildren have started to look at you and to do sums. You have buried all of that class now, one by one. {npc} is at your elbow, who is new, and young, and who was told about you by the last one. {He} hands you a cup.

choices.text: Tell them the truth, as far as they can take it: it runs in the family

effects.log: Some of them stare. There is a very old woman, who says "I always knew it," and who is never asked what exactly was known. People start bringing you their old stories to check. It is a sort of job, and you are getting quite good at it.

choices.text: Go home, and put some ash in your hair

effects.log: You put in some ash, and you learn to stoop, and to forget names. {npc} helps you with the ash. You have been a very convincing old person, for about a hundred years now. People tell you that you are doing wonderfully, at your age.

events.text: {npc} has found a grey hair, and {he} is holding it up to the lamp. It is {his} own. {He} looks at it, and then {he} looks across at you, with your plain dark head. "I would like an answer," {he} says, "some time this year. And I know that you are going to say that you are thinking about it."

choices.text: Tell {him}. How long you expect to live, and all the rest of it

effects.log: You do it within the hour, which may be a record. {He} takes it in, with {his} chin in {his} hand. "So I am the one who will get to leave," {he} says. {He} thinks about that. "Well, you can bury me, and you had better be on time." You go and sit very close to {him}.

choices.text: Say that it is only good food, and clean living

effects.log: {He} looks at you for a good while. "Yes," {he} says, and {he} drops the hair in the fire. You do not need telling what number you heard, just then, behind your ear. You learn to sleep on the side of the bed that faces away.

events.text: {npc} is sitting in the yard. It has come on to rain. {He} has been watching a snail for a whole morning. "It got to the wall," {he} says, very much satisfied. You know what they will call {him} at school. Behind {his} ear there is something else, you can tell, that is not happy with the snail.

choices.text: Sit down in the rain. Teach {him} to tell the two of them apart

effects.log: You sit down. "Which one is that?" you say, and it takes {him} until the spring. {He} is a very good student. It will not be easy for {him}, and you will be around to see it, and for a long time after that.

choices.text: Pick {him} up, and take {him} in. Tell {him} to run about with the others

effects.log: You set {him} down at the door and give {him} a push. {He} runs. It takes some doing. The others let {him} hold the coats. {He} looks back at the wall, you notice, every so often, while nobody is watching.

events.text: {npc} has come to the district with a very small brazier in a very clean bag. {He} reads shells for the court. A shell tells you what will fall and when, and {he} has burned nine hundred. They do not all tell the same thing, and that has begun to trouble {him}. {He} would like to look at your back. Only to look. {He} is in no hurry.

choices.text: Put the brazier on {his} head, as a beginning

ok.log: It does not hurt {him} much. You see {him} out through the door, in a shower of coals. {He} picks up the bag on the road, and {he} brushes it off. "I see," {he} says, bowing, as if you had told {him} something. {He} writes it down.

fail.log: {He} is older than {he} looks and very well-informed. {He} knows just where the plates meet. You lie on the floor of the inn, unable to get your breath for the first time ever. {He} has a look, and then {he} helps you up. {He} is really very grateful.

choices.text: Say you will think it over, and that {he} may call in a year or two

effects.log: {He} is delighted. Nobody has ever said that to {him}. "I shall," {he} says. {He} does, on the very day, to the hour. You have not finished thinking. So {he} takes a room in the district, and {he} sets up the brazier, and {he} waits.

events.text: {npc} is very old now, and {he} has been carried here in a chair. You have not much changed. {He} has the same small brazier, and {his} hands will hardly hold it. "I read it again last night," {he} says. "My last shell. It said you would come to me, in the end, and lay your back in the fire of your own will. I have waited thirty years on that. I can see that I was wrong. I should so like to know what you say."

choices.text: End it. Take the brazier out of {his} hands, and put it in the river

ok.log: It takes hardly anything. {He} is as light as a basket. You put out the coals, and you sink the bag, and you carry {him} to {his} bed. {He} is crying with rage, or something like it. You know you have robbed {him} of the only thing that {he} ever wanted.

fail.log: {He} has kept one thing back for thirty years, and {he} has it in {his} sleeve. It goes into a seam in your back, and you can smell it. You get the chair over, and you get out of there. It will be a long time closing, and {he} has seen what {he} came to see.

choices.text: Take off your shirt. Let {him} touch it, with {his} hands, and no fire

effects.log: You kneel down with your back to {him}. {He} does nothing for a long while. {His} fingers are dry, and they go slowly along each seam, as one reads in the dark. "Oh," {he} says. "It is all still there." In the morning {he} is gone from the chair, with a look of having been told.

events.text: You sit down on the bank to fix a sandal. Someone comes and shakes you, and it is {npc}, and you say that you will only be a moment. But the sandal has rotted. There is grass growing through your fingers. It is spring, and it was autumn. The river goes by you on both sides, and it is cold, and it would be so easy not to get up. {He} has got you by the wrist.

choices.text: Sit a little longer. Go on in, up to the neck

effects.log: You go in. A whole winter goes through you, and you feel it pass, the way you might feel a cart in the road. You come out knowing how far the river is from the sea, in your back. {npc} is a good deal greyer. It is very hard to feel as sorry as you should.

choices.text: Get up. Sleep in a hard bed, near a road, and let people wake you

effects.log: You rent a room above a stable, by the market. It is very loud. It is the worst year of your life. You get up every morning when you are told, and you are on time for everything, and {npc} comes and looks at you, and nods.

events.text: There are soldiers in the valley, and two hundred people on the shoal, in the middle of winter, and the boats have gone. You have got a place in the last boat. You can feel the river from here, in your whole back, the deep part and where it could be crossed. If somebody were to go and stand in it, somebody who is very hard to kill. They would need to stay for a long time.

choices.text: Get out of the boat

effects.log: Nobody ever knows quite what they walked on, in that dark, with a rope in their hands. A log, they say. It took three nights. You do not feel your legs until the thaw. {npc} finds you, wedged in the bank. {He} has got a very bad cough, and {he} has brought you a dry coat.

choices.text: Stay in the boat. You were told that it would go

effects.log: It goes. It is a well-run boat, and you get to the far side, and you find a good dry barn. You hear it being told later on, from far along the road. Behind your ear, somebody has started to count, and you cannot make them stop.

events.text: {npc} takes you north, in the cold season, to a ford that has no name. There is a flat stone on this bank, worn down in one place by someone sitting. It looks like a shoal out there. You wait. On the ninth day, one end of the shoal opens an eye. A thin black head comes up beside it, looks you over, and says, "You are late." It is {bk_anc}, or the half of it that talks. The other half will say so in time.

choices.text: Ask what you came all this way to ask. Was it worth it, to carry anyone?

effects.log: "Ask the big one," says the snake. "I could tell you, but you would believe me." So you ask. You say it to the eye, slowly, twice. The eye closes. It opens. You wait there until the snow, and {npc} takes you home. You are told that you may expect an answer.

choices.text: Ask nothing. Sit down on the stone, and tell it the news

effects.log: You tell it who is dead, and who owes what. You go through the whole family, name by name, for as long as you have breath. The snake listens with one eye. It corrects your dates. {npc} is asleep. It seems you did know how this is done.

events.text: You wake one morning, and there is something on your landing, the size of a hill. It is two hundred li from the north river. There is a long trail behind it, through three counties. It has been walking for eight years. {npc} comes out in {his} night things. {bk_anc} looks at you with one eye. Very, very slowly, it begins to bring its head down.

choices.text: Stay. Take the whole of its answer

effects.log: It nods. That is all that it is. It nods once, and it takes the whole morning. Whatever it was that you said on that bank eight years ago, or did not say, you have got your answer. "It wanted to tell you in person," says the snake. It sounds embarrassed.

choices.text: Climb up on its back. It has come a long way for that

effects.log: It lets you. It does not do anything else. You sit up there, with your hands on the plates, and you can feel every one who has ever sat there, in the wear of it. {npc} calls up to ask if you are coming down for breakfast, and you will, in a while.

events.text: {npc} has been telling you something for some days. "You keep going out like a lamp," {he} says. "Half the time you are in the river, and the other half you are looking at it." You could go up to the dry hill country, and hurry, and get old. You could go in. {He} rubs {his} face. There is one other way, {he} supposes. You would have to be in no hurry about it.

choices.text: Go up to the dry country. Learn to hurry

effects.log: It takes you a year to get there, and it is worth it. Up on the hills, the wind blows, and nothing has any depth to it. Behind your ear, one of them has gone very quiet, and the other one has started to say, "Well? Well?" You find that you are walking quite fast.

choices.text: Go in. Do not come back up for anyone but the one in the water

effects.log: You leave your coat on the stone, folded. {npc} is still talking. You walk down until it closes over you, and it is very cold, and everything slows, and stops, and goes on. The two of you turn, and you look at each other, for the first time.

choices.text: Keep the ford. Stand in it. One foot on each side

effects.log: Nobody has ever kept a ferry and a winter sleep and a bad temper all at once. {npc} reckons that it takes a certain kind of person, and that there was somebody once who did come down to the stone every tenth day.

events.text: You have missed a ferry. You ran for it, with your bundle bouncing and your knees going, and you missed it by the length of a pole, and you stood there with your heart going like a mill, shouting. Your hair is coming in grey, and you have got a bad knee. {npc} comes up behind you, puffing. "Well, that is it," {he} says. "There is another one tomorrow." You could not be more pleased.

choices.text: Be early, for everything, for the rest of your life

effects.log: You are up before the hens. You sit at the ferry stage for an hour, with your bundle, and you tap your foot. People find you a great nuisance, and you are, and you have got so much to do and so little time.

choices.text: Answer letters on the same day. Say yes, and no, and do it

effects.log: It frightens people. You say yes to the Ohs' cousin, and you buy a field, and you sell it, and you are wrong about both. You have never had such a good time. The matchmaker's grandchild says that you must be feeling unwell.

events.text: You come up, by the old stone, with some news. {npc} has been dead for a while, the snake says. There is somebody else on the stone, about the same size, with a jar. Your people go on coming down on the tenth day, as they have for a long time. They tell you who has died. You do not always know who that is. You know them all, as they were. You have got them all in your back, and there is plenty of room.

choices.text: Come up for the one in the water, whoever they are

effects.log: A woodcutter, and a tax clerk, and somebody's goat. You do not ask. What you carry is your own, and it is getting to be a large family. The snake says that it will not fit in the record, and it has found a way to fit it.

choices.text: Lie on the bottom, and let the two of them talk, for a century or so

effects.log: They have never had the chance to go through it properly. The snake has its dates. The tortoise, as far as you can tell, has one word, and it uses it about once every eleven years. It has been a very satisfying discussion.

events.text: You keep the ferry. It is the slowest on the river, and it is never full. In the winter you tell {npc} that you are going to see about something, and you go down the bank in your good coat, and you come back when the ice goes out, with some weed in your hair. "You missed the wedding," says {npc}. "Whose?" you ask. {He} tells you, and you have got to think back, and then you do remember. You owe them a pig.

choices.text: Run the ferry in any weather. Nobody has ever been lost

effects.log: People have started to come a long way round to cross with you. It takes all day. You do not charge the first time. There are some who think it is on account of your prayers. You let your back do the steering.

choices.text: Take the pig round. It is only eleven years late

effects.log: They are very polite about it. There is some question of who the pig is for. You stay for a bit, and you eat something. By the time that you go home, you are told you must stay for the hundred-day feast of the next lot.

events.text: You are the oldest thing in the district, after the zelkova, and you are listed with it. Young mothers bring babies for you to look at. You look at them. It is said to be lucky. You have just been thinking about what to say to the mother of the last baby, who was very worried, and you say it now. "It will be fine," you say. It has been nineteen years.

choices.text: Laugh. It takes you a while to see the joke

effects.log: You see it in the summer. People hear you, all the way down at the mill. They come up to see what the matter is, and you are not able to tell them, for it is a very long story, and there is a lot about a pear tree in it.

choices.text: Have them send for the child, to see if you were right

effects.log: A big red-eared carter arrives, rather shy. You have a good long look. "Yes," you tell {npc}, in the end, "it is fine." {He} has a bad shoulder. Nobody thinks that it is odd of you to tell {him} that it will mend, and it does, by and by.

events.text: You sit out on the stone by the water most days now, with your feet in it. {npc} comes down with your rice, and {he} sits with you. Somebody is walking across the ford, with a bundle on their head, and you watch them all the way over. It takes them hardly any time at all. Behind your ear, someone starts to give a number. You have asked it for years, and it has never once said. You lift your hand, slowly.

choices.text: Let it say. You would like to know, now

effects.log: It says. It is a very small number. It is quite a kind voice. You think about that, for as long as you have got, which is, you are told, a little while. "Yes," you say. "In a moment."

choices.text: Tell it no. Eat your rice, and ask {npc} for the news

effects.log: {He} tells you who has died and who owes what. It goes on for some time. The sun moves across the water. You did not know that there was so much of it. You nod at the end of it, or you are going to.
